title: The Ophan's arrival: seven questions
eyebrow: Design area: the demand loop · the Ophan's arrival (#418) · nothing built

short.lead: The Ophan arriving in the last 60 seconds and catching players (#418) is already approved, but a few details were never decided. I stopped before writing any code so you can make these calls. Each question has options with my suggestion marked, and you can always give your own answer. The warning that it's coming (#434) isn't on this page: that one is yours to design from scratch, and until then the build leaves an empty slot for it.
short.hint: Tap a card for what's already settled or what one question decides.
items: It arrives 60 seconds before the portal closes (HuntWindowSeconds in the tuning file).
It comes only on raids where a demand is due or still owed.
Caught carrying the demanded piece, it takes the piece and you live. Caught empty-handed, you die.
Once it takes the piece it leaves at once, so one holder saves everyone.
It's 9.6 m tall and drifts through walls.
The Ophan's model, its rig and five animations: arrive (unfolding out of a point of light), hover and turn, advance, fix its gaze, and take.
The Wick's whole catch path: a catch that kills, the death showing on every machine, spectating, and the whole party going down.
The tuning file from #433 and the raid clock.
A flag on loot marking six pieces as artifacts: the Gold Death Mask, Arm Reliquary, Gilded Altarpiece, Jewelled Hat Badge, Nautilus Cup and Ancient Relic.
1. Which piece counts as wanted, for now
The demand itself (#419) comes later, so something has to stand in for it.
2. Who it fixes its eye on
With two players in the raid, which one it goes after.
The spot its point of light opens.
Your 2026-10-15 answer, written for a 90-second hunt, now has to fit 60 seconds.
Your 2026-10-21 issue says to show the Ophan in the sky instead of hunting you; the demand loop has it hunting.
6. What it does after killing someone
Whether it keeps going after the others.
7. Whether it ships before its warning
Its warning (#434) is yours to design. The question is whether the arrival can go into staging before that, with an empty slot where the warning will go.

choices: wanted
Until the demand exists, which carried piece does it take?
A
Any of the six pieces already marked as artifacts
Uses the artifact flag that's already on loot. When the demand (#419) lands, it narrows to the demanded piece.
B
Only one piece that a test switch names
Closest to the real demand, but only reachable through the test switch for now.
C
None yet: build only the kill, and add the take when #419 lands
Simplest now, but the 'you live if you carry it' half waits.
It makes the whole rule playable today with no new data, and #419 swaps in the real demand later.
target
With two players, who does it fix its eye on?
A
The nearest player, switching only when that one is caught or leaves
Predictable, so the other player can draw it away.
B
Whoever carries the most
Greed gets punished, and players think about who holds what.
C
Someone chosen at random
Unpredictable, and nobody can plan for it.
Being nearest is something players can see and play around, which suits co-op.
where
Where does it arrive?
A
A point of light a set distance from its target, through the walls
It's always close enough to matter, wherever the players are.
B
At the arrival portal
Players far from the portal get a head start.
C
In the middle of the castle
A fixed place players can learn.
It keeps the last minute tense wherever the players are, with the distance as one number to tune.
speed
How fast does it move?
A
2.5 m/s on arrival, rising to the players' 5 m/s by 30 seconds left
Your 2026-10-15 numbers, squeezed into the 60-second window. The speeds go on the Ophan itself, so the tuning file keeps exactly the fields you approved.
B
The same numbers, but added to the tuning file
All the demand numbers stay in one place, which means adding fields you didn't approve in #433.
C
Your own numbers
Tell me the speeds.
It keeps your own numbers and adds nothing to the approved tuning file.
sky
Your 2026-10-21 issue (#430) shows the Ophan in the sky instead of hunting you. Which wins for now?
A
The demand loop's hunt wins for now; the sky idea is saved for later, such as the final battle
#430 stays open as a later idea.
B
The sky idea wins: it watches from above and doesn't hunt
#418 changes shape before anything is built.
C
Both: it shows in the sky first, then comes down to hunt
More to build, and more presence before the hunt.
You approved the hunting demand loop after #430, so it looks like the later call; this just confirms it.
after
After it kills an empty-handed player, what does it do?
A
Keeps hunting the others until the portal closes
Only a paid piece sends it away.
B
Leaves, satisfied by the kill
One death buys everyone else's escape.
It matches your rule that only the piece sends it away.
warn
Can the arrival go into staging before you've designed its warning?
A
Yes: build it with an empty slot, and add the warning when you've designed it
The loop keeps moving, and nothing about the warning gets decided for you.
B
No: build and test it on its own branch, but keep it out of staging until the warning is in
Staging never has an Ophan that arrives unannounced.
It keeps the loop moving, and the slot makes adding the warning later a small change.

wrapup.summary: Seven details of the Ophan's arrival, each with options and my suggestion marked.
wrapup.changing: Nothing is built yet. The branch is cut and waiting.
wrapup.blocking: Your answers to the seven choices.
wrapup.next: Once you answer, I build #418 on its own branch and test it. Choice 7 decides whether it then goes into staging.
